title: Codex Browser Control: browser actions that expire when the page changes
audience: Teams that need browser automation to bind every mutation to the exact page state a person reviewed.
promise: Observe a synthetic itinerary, propose one harmless preference change, require exact approval, verify the fresh state, and refuse the stale plan after the page moves.
story: A labeled synthetic travel page exposes one reversible seat-preference control and a local itinerary-change trigger.
The intended provider flow binds the plan to the target's semantic identity and page digest before any apply.
A single-use approval names the mutation, scope, expiry, and current state; independent verification reads the changed value back.
When the itinerary changes, the semantic target becomes stale and the old plan must stop before mutation.
verified_locally: The self-contained fixture has no network calls, credentials, payment controls, account data, or external mutations.
The source-aligned semantic target, harmless reversible select action, stale mutation, and target_changed refusal are recorded.
The current dirty checkout passes lint, typecheck, tests, build, and MCP smoke gates.
The 1600x900 preview is rendered from the synthetic case and visually inspected.
open_gates: Reload the matching extension/native-host pair with explicit deployment approval and capture a valid CB-2 observe-to-plan receipt.
Capture the exact CB-3 approval, apply, verify, and stale-refusal receipts on the disposable local origin.
Verify a hosted no-auth case URL and external destination readbacks.
claim_boundary: This packet proves a labeled synthetic browser fixture, source contract, and local candidate visual. It does not claim an installed extension round trip, side-panel approval, browser mutation, verification, stale refusal, hosting, or publication.
